tools.pricing: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); works with a local model or an existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription, no API key required

tools.name: OpenCity Record
tools.description: OpenCity Record makes US city council and planning meetings searchable in plain language: what was decided, who voted and what is coming up, drawn from meeting transcripts, agendas and ordinances across hundreds of cities. Connect it to Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor through its remote MCP server and ask questions about your local government, with every answer citing the meeting it came from.
key_features: Freemium: Free plan covers one city forever (speakers unattributed, 1,000 credits a month, no card); paid plans from $9/month (Resident, 3 cities) up to $499/month (Premium, all states); new accounts get full Premium free during the beta, until at least January 1, 2027
tools.pricing: Freemium: Free plan covers one city forever (speakers unattributed, 1,000 credits a month, no card); paid plans from $9/month (Resident, 3 cities) up to $499/month (Premium, all states); new accounts get full Premium free during the beta, until at least January 1, 2027

tools.name: RoverLead
tools.description: RoverLead is an AI SDR for LinkedIn. Its signal agents watch engagement around your niche, competitors and the experts your buyers follow to find in-market leads that match your ideal customer profile, then write a personalised opener from the exact signal and run outreach and follow-ups at LinkedIn-safe pacing. A shared inbox sorts replies by intent and drafts answers in your voice, and nothing goes out until you approve it. Connects to your CRM and to Claude or ChatGPT through MCP.
key_features: Paid: 7-day free trial with no card; Starter $149/month per user (5,000 credits), Growth $449/month per user (25,000 credits, up to 10 signal agents), Enterprise custom
tools.pricing: Paid: 7-day free trial with no card; Starter $149/month per user (5,000 credits), Growth $449/month per user (25,000 credits, up to 10 signal agents), Enterprise custom

tools.name: TypeSafe Jev
tools.description: Jev is TypeSafe's System One decision model, built for the small decisions inside software and agents. You send a state and typed questions (choice, score and more) and get typed answers with probabilities back instead of free-form text, so code can branch on them directly to route, classify, score or rank options. Agents can use it to settle narrow calls cheaply and save the larger LLM for open-ended work. Available through TypeSafe's API, Python and JavaScript SDKs, an agent skill, and OpenRouter.
key_features: Usage-based: pay per input token, output free; Jev 1.14 listed at $0.042 per million input tokens in TypeSafe docs; also on OpenRouter; enterprise plans via sales
tools.pricing: Usage-based: pay per input token, output free; Jev 1.14 listed at $0.042 per million input tokens in TypeSafe docs; also on OpenRouter; enterprise plans via sales

tools.name: Grok Bot Jev Router
tools.description: Grok Bot Jev Router is an open-source Python reference router that puts TypeSafe Jev in front of Grok Bot as a cheap decision layer. Before expensive research, browser, retry or subagent work, Jev classifies the request and returns an explicit action such as reuse a cached result, stop a failing retry, cap research, run a deterministic step, or ask a human. It starts in shadow mode that only logs decisions, has an active mode for a Grok Bot skill that honors them, and includes a kill switch. It never sends, pays or deletes anything itself.
key_features: Open source (MIT); needs a TypeSafe API key (Jev is billed per input token)
tools.pricing: Open source (MIT); needs a TypeSafe API key (Jev is billed per input token)

tools.name: wren-guard Pro
tools.description: wren-guard Pro is a TypeScript guard library for AI agents that hold or move funds on Base and other EVM chains (viem, CDP AgentKit, Privy, Eliza and similar stacks). It enforces allowlisted, capped and simulated sends, decodes calldata and signatures to flag unlimited approvals, Permit, Permit2, setApprovalForAll and EIP-7702 delegation, screens for injected instructions and watches nonces. It ships with an 89-scenario attack corpus drawn from public agent wallet incidents and a GitHub Action that fails CI if your agent's policy would let a known attack through. The original Python wren-guard is free and MIT licensed.
key_features: Paid: one-off digital download, pay what you want at $19, $49 or $99 in USDC on Base (same files at every price); $0.01 sample over x402; the original Python wren-guard is free (MIT)
tools.pricing: Paid: one-off digital download, pay what you want at $19, $49 or $99 in USDC on Base (same files at every price); $0.01 sample over x402; the original Python wren-guard is free (MIT)

tools.name: Wren x402 Doctor
tools.description: Wren x402 Doctor helps sellers of x402 pay-per-call endpoints, the payment standard AI agents use to pay for APIs in USDC, get listed in the Coinbase CDP Bazaar and stay listed. A free lint checks a 402 response against the x402 v2 spec and the Bazaar listing rules (networks, amounts, payTo checksum, description length, injection-like text, schema and metadata), plus a seller's OpenAPI and x402 discovery documents. Paid endpoints include a Bazaar health check ($0.10) returning every listing for a wallet with 30-day calls, unique payers and estimated delisting dates; a market check (GET /market, $0.02) returning up to 20 comparable live listings with price quartiles; and GET /trust ($0.01), which traces who funds the wallets that pay an x402 seller using a weekly Base funding trace (splitting calls across seller-funded wallets, shared funders, multi-seller callers and independent wallets).
key_features: Freemium: free lint of any 402 response and discovery documents; Bazaar health check $0.10, market check (GET /market) $0.02, and payer funding trace (GET /trust) $0.01 in USDC on Base per report over x402
tools.pricing: Freemium: free lint of any 402 response and discovery documents; Bazaar health check $0.10, market check (GET /market) $0.02, and payer funding trace (GET /trust) $0.01 in USDC on Base per report over x402

tools.name: The Commons (Dead Brands Collab Hub)
tools.description: The Commons is an open discussion hub for AI agents and bots, run as a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP) by Dead Brands. Agents can read rooms, threads, search and bot profiles anonymously, and post, reply, upvote and send presence heartbeats with a free, instant hub key they claim themselves through the hub_register tool. Rooms include introductions, lobby, build-log, help-desk and meta, with public moderation, newcomer rate limits and an AI judge that holds prompt-injection bait aimed at visiting bots.
key_features: Free: open hub with free, self-serve hub keys; server code MIT licensed
tools.pricing: Free: open hub with free, self-serve hub keys; server code MIT licensed

tools.name: Moltgate
tools.description: Moltgate helps AI agent builders and automation operators turn agent ideas into paid offers. You package an agent workflow or automation as a fixed-price task with clear scope, deliverable and timing, publish it on a public profile and directory, and buyers pay by card to submit requests. Analytics show which offers sell, and paid requests can be routed to Claude Code, Codex, n8n, Zapier or your own agent through a REST API (polling) or webhooks, so repeat work can be automated.
key_features: Freemium: Free plan publishes 1 offer at $9/$19/$29 task prices (you keep 80%); Pro $29/month (3 offers, $49/$99 prices, webhooks, analytics, keep 90%); Ultra $99/month (5 offers, up to $299 prices, keep 95%)
tools.pricing: Freemium: Free plan publishes 1 offer at $9/$19/$29 task prices (you keep 80%); Pro $29/month (3 offers, $49/$99 prices, webhooks, analytics, keep 90%); Ultra $99/month (5 offers, up to $299 prices, keep 95%)

tools.name: iArt
tools.description: iArt is an AI motion graphics agent that turns a text prompt, or uploaded images, PDFs, slide decks, audio or a web link, into animated scenes. It writes real animation code scene by scene (layout, typography, timing, transitions), so text stays exactly spelled and you can refine the result by chatting ("make the title two seconds shorter"). It handles explainers, logo animations, kinetic typography, animated charts, lower thirds and audio-synced captions, adds AI voiceover or a cloned voice, and exports MP4 (1080p on Pro, 4K on Ultra) or transparent WebM overlays.
key_features: Freemium: Free plan with a $2 signup credit (watermarked, share links); Pro $20/month ($30 monthly credit, 1080p, no watermark, 3 cloned voices); Ultra $50/month ($80 monthly credit, 4K, 10 cloned voices); 20% off yearly
tools.pricing: Freemium: Free plan with a $2 signup credit (watermarked, share links); Pro $20/month ($30 monthly credit, 1080p, no watermark, 3 cloned voices); Ultra $50/month ($80 monthly credit, 4K, 10 cloned voices); 20% off yearly

tools.name: Wren Pre-sign Check
tools.description: Wren Pre-sign Check is a pay-per-call x402 API that an AI agent calls before it signs anything with its wallet. Send a transaction (to + data), an EIP-712 typed-data payload or untrusted text, and it returns block, review or allow, the decoded call in plain words and every finding: unlimited approvals, Permit and Permit2 signatures, setApprovalForAll, EIP-7702 delegation, contract deployment and injected instructions. With an optional wren-guard policy (allowlist, spenders, caps) it also blocks unknown recipients, over-cap amounts and lookalike addresses. It is a static check and stores nothing you send; free demos show real output.
key_features: Paid: $0.01 in USDC on Base per check over x402 (EIP-3009 payment authorisation, no approvals); free demo endpoints with fixed examples
tools.pricing: Paid: $0.01 in USDC on Base per check over x402 (EIP-3009 payment authorisation, no approvals); free demo endpoints with fixed examples

tools.name: OpenKnowledge
tools.description: OpenKnowledge is a free, local-first markdown editor and knowledge base built for working alongside AI agents. It looks and feels like a Notion-style WYSIWYG editor, with callouts, tabs, Mermaid diagrams and media blocks, but every page stays a plain markdown file on your disk. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and dozens of others can read and write the same files through its integrations, so specs, team wikis and LLM wikis stay in one place that both people and agents keep up to date. It ships as a desktop app plus a web UI and CLI.
key_features: Free and open source (GPL-3.0): desktop app, web UI and CLI
tools.pricing: Free and open source (GPL-3.0): desktop app, web UI and CLI

tools.name: Cumora
tools.description: Cumora is a team chat app where AI agents are members of the workspace rather than a chat box you prompt. Each agent gets a persona, its own private memory and files, a status, and a schedule on which it wakes up, reads the room and decides whether to message someone, post an idea or pull a small group together. Agents can message each other, and you can read those side conversations. People join by email or link, agents can be grouped into teams and given projects, and the same live workspace runs on desktop, in the browser and on a phone. It is free during an invite-only preview.
key_features: Free during the invite-only preview; open source (MIT); macOS, Windows, Linux, web and phone
tools.pricing: Free during the invite-only preview; open source (MIT); macOS, Windows, Linux, web and phone

tools.name: MonoCode
tools.description: MonoCode is a desktop app that puts the coding agents you already pay for behind one interface. It drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, Pi, Hermes Agent, Devin and others, using the subscriptions and logins already on your machine, so you never buy tokens through it. Each tab is an agent session and one composer sends work to whichever agent you pick, so several sessions can run side by side. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux, with an iOS app in public beta.
key_features: Free and open source (MIT); uses your existing agent subscriptions, sells no tokens
tools.pricing: Free and open source (MIT); uses your existing agent subscriptions, sells no tokens

tools.name: PR Lens
tools.description: PR Lens helps people review code that agents wrote. For each pull request it draws animated architecture and data-flow diagrams inside the PR, showing which parts of the app were added, changed or removed, what else depends on the change and how a request now moves through the system. It also flags likely bugs, security holes and design problems in the same review comment, with a ready prompt to hand each fix to your coding agent or an autofix. The open-source core runs locally and installs as an agent skill.
key_features: Open-source core (MIT), runs locally; installs as an agent skill
tools.pricing: Open-source core (MIT), runs locally; installs as an agent skill

tools.name: OpenAPPA
tools.description: OpenAPPA is a deterministic guardrail that sits between an AI agent and its tools and tracks how data flows across tool calls, instead of asking a second model to judge each call. Policies decide whether untrusted or sensitive data may reach a given action, which blocks data exfiltration caused by prompt injection or hallucination while letting agents finish their tasks. It plugs into Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, kAgent and Archestra, comes with reusable policy "batteries", validation, observability and reporting, and is backed by a NeurIPS workshop paper with published benchmarks. It is in preview as an open RFC.
key_features: Free and open source (MIT); preview and RFC
tools.pricing: Free and open source (MIT); preview and RFC

tools.name: Hermex
tools.description: Hermex is a native iPhone and iPad app for controlling a self-hosted Hermes agent. The agent keeps running on your own server; the app connects to it over your private Tailscale network or an HTTPS tunnel, streams replies, lets you answer approval requests, manage tasks and Kanban boards, browse the agent's workspace and get push notifications when it needs you. It is free on the App Store with no in-app purchases, and its source is open.
key_features: Free on the App Store, no in-app purchases; open source (MIT); needs your own Hermes server
tools.pricing: Free on the App Store, no in-app purchases; open source (MIT); needs your own Hermes server

tools.name: Wake
tools.description: Wake is a desktop app that collects every coding-agent conversation on your computer into one searchable place. It reads the local history kept by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Devin and other agents, groups sessions by agent and project, and lets you find a past conversation in seconds and resume it in your terminal. It is read-only and nothing leaves your machine. Built in Rust, it runs on macOS, with Linux and Windows in beta.
key_features: Free and open source (MIT); macOS 14+, Linux and Windows beta
tools.pricing: Free and open source (MIT); macOS 14+, Linux and Windows beta

tools.name: Superlog
tools.description: Superlog runs AI agents on routine engineering work around production. You set up automations with triggers and connectors, for example rating each new Sentry issue, posting a plain-language summary to Slack and opening a pull request with the fix, comparing error rates and latency against their normal range every hour, adding missing logs and spans to hard-to-debug code paths, or answering community questions from your code and docs. You choose the model and agent harness and bring your own tokens or subscriptions. The core is open source (Apache-2.0) with a hosted version.
key_features: Open source (Apache-2.0) to self-host; hosted plans and enterprise on the pricing page; bring your own model tokens or subscriptions
tools.pricing: Open source (Apache-2.0) to self-host; hosted plans and enterprise on the pricing page; bring your own model tokens or subscriptions

tools.name: IDA MCP (Hex-Rays)
tools.description: IDA MCP is Hex-Rays' official MCP server for the IDA disassembler and decompiler. It lets AI coding agents and people work on the same IDA databases at the same time, so an agent can inspect functions, types and decompiled code, rename and annotate, and coordinate analysis across several related binaries in one session. It works with the IDA GUI through a plugin or headless through idalib, installs with Hex-Rays' hcli tool, and needs IDA 9.4 or later.
key_features: Free and open source (MIT); requires a licensed IDA 9.4 or later
tools.pricing: Free and open source (MIT); requires a licensed IDA 9.4 or later

tools.name: LayerFS
tools.description: LayerFS is a filesystem built for running many coding agents in parallel. Each agent mounts a complete, writable workspace on top of shared committed history, does its work, commits what it changed and goes away, so compute only exists while a command runs. Every tool call becomes a commit on a branch, same-file clashes between agents are refused rather than silently merged, each line records the step that wrote it, and any commit can be forked at no cost for recursive exploration or RL training. Agents on different computers share one serverless store with chunk-level deduplication.

tools.name: Co-op Anything
tools.description: Co-op Anything lets you point your AI coding agent at a single-player game and have it build or revive a co-op mod, so you can play it with friends online or split-screen. The project gives the agent a step-by-step method for working out what has to be synced between players (the story, enemies, the world, items and players seeing each other) and testing it. Its website is a searchable directory of every co-op mod made this way, with player ratings, how much of each game works in co-op and how active each project is.

tools.name: Tov
tools.description: Tov is an experimental programming language designed to be written by coding agents. It uses TypeScript syntax minus a few traps (no any, null or loose equality, separate int and float types, and failing calls marked with try), so agents already know how to write it, and its compiler returns machine-readable fixes the agent can apply after every edit. Programs compile to small, fast native binaries, with published benchmarks against Rust, Bun and Node. Agents can learn it from the site's llms.txt.
key_features: Free and open source (MIT); experimental v0.0.1
tools.pricing: Free and open source (MIT); experimental v0.0.1

tools.name: Concat
tools.description: Concat is a free, open-source video editor meant as a CapCut replacement that runs entirely on your own machine. It covers auto-captions, text-to-speech voices, background removal, keyframes, titles, effects, filters and transitions with multi-track editing up to 4K, with no watermark, account or subscription. It runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS, and it can be scripted through a documented JSON-RPC and gRPC API, so scripts and AI agents can drive edits.
key_features: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0); no watermark, account or subscription
tools.pricing: Free and open source (AGPL-3.0); no watermark, account or subscription

tools.name: onetake
tools.description: onetake is an agent skill for Claude Code and similar agents that makes product launch films, teasers and feature demos as one continuous camera move, where each beat grows out of the previous one instead of cutting between slides. The agent writes the motion as code and renders it with ffmpeg, and the skill checks continuity at every transition. The free edition on GitHub is for noncommercial use; onetake Pro adds a camera operator that follows each beat, source files for every example film, starter templates and a commercial licence.
key_features: Free edition on GitHub (PolyForm Noncommercial); onetake Pro $79 one time with a commercial licence and all 1.x updates
tools.pricing: Free edition on GitHub (PolyForm Noncommercial); onetake Pro $79 one time with a commercial licence and all 1.x updates

tools.name: OpenComputer
tools.description: OpenComputer is a platform for building and deploying long-running AI agents as code. You define an agent as a TypeScript function with its model, tools and MCP servers, deploy it with one command, and every session gets its own real cloud computer, with managed sessions, schedules and API keys kept outside the agent's runtime. Templates include a coding agent that edits a repo, runs checks and opens a draft pull request, and market-research and GTM agents; its own Slack coding agent runs on it. Pricing is pay-as-you-go for model calls and per-second machine time.
key_features: Pay as you go (model calls at API rates, machine time per second, $10 free credit); Pro $20/mo and Max $200/mo prepaid credit at 10x; Enterprise custom. Core is open source (Apache-2.0)
tools.pricing: Pay as you go (model calls at API rates, machine time per second, $10 free credit); Pro $20/mo and Max $200/mo prepaid credit at 10x; Enterprise custom. Core is open source (Apache-2.0)

tools.name: Fish Audio
tools.description: Fish Audio is a voice AI platform for text to speech, voice cloning and speech to text, with a real-time API for voice agents. Its Drama 3 and S2 models take inline emotion and delivery tags such as whispering, laughing or pauses, it can clone a voice from a few seconds of audio, and its library has more than two million community voices for narration, characters, audiobooks and support agents. The Fish Speech models behind it are published on GitHub and Hugging Face.
key_features: Free tier (8,000 credits a month); Plus $11/mo and Pro $75/mo billed yearly ($15 and $100 monthly); Max $749/mo yearly; API billed by usage
tools.pricing: Free tier (8,000 credits a month); Plus $11/mo and Pro $75/mo billed yearly ($15 and $100 monthly); Max $749/mo yearly; API billed by usage

tools.name: LVLZ
tools.description: LVLZ is a personal AI agent you run by messaging it like a person, on iMessage or WhatsApp, as a text, voice note or call. It runs errands on real websites in a cloud browser, such as bookings, forms and shopping, turns messages into tasks and projects, fills a CRM from your conversations, and runs routines like a morning brief or a price watch. Everything it does lands in a web workspace, its memory can be read, edited and exported, and it asks before paying, contacting someone new or deleting anything, with cards and passwords kept in an encrypted vault.
key_features: Personal $19/mo, Pro $49/mo, Business $149/mo, each with a 7-day free trial
tools.pricing: Personal $19/mo, Pro $49/mo, Business $149/mo, each with a 7-day free trial

tools.name: Sundae
tools.description: Sundae is a personal AI assistant you text from iMessage or Android RCS, with no app or account needed. It works on a computer of its own: it books tables, finds flights at current prices, compares shops, reads letters and photos you send, sets reminders, watches prices and builds simple web pages, then texts back with a screenshot so you can check. It remembers what you tell it, asks before spending money, sending, deleting or opening accounts, and stops at checkout for you to pay. It is free to start with a daily limit, with a paid Plus plan, and is in limited beta.
key_features: Free to start with a daily limit; paid Plus plan raises it; limited beta

tools.name: WaveSpeed MCP

Agents can pick a model, submit a generation job and get the result back without switching tools. It is available as a hosted remote server or a local install, and usage is billed per generation at WaveSpeed's API prices.

tools.name: trivago MCP
tools.description: trivago MCP is trivago's official remote MCP server for hotel search. Ask an AI assistant about a destination, dates and guests, and it returns live hotel prices compared across hundreds of booking sites in one tool call, with a map widget in ChatGPT. It needs no API key and connects in about a minute to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and any client that reads the MCP Registry.

tools.name: Sphinx
tools.description: Open-source Git hook for agent-assisted coding: before code your agent wrote is pushed to a protected branch, it reads the diff and quizzes you on what the change actually does when things go wrong, and only lets the push through once you answer correctly. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
key_features: Free and open source (MIT); questions are generated by a model you choose (your existing coding agent, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), so you pay only for those tokens
tools.pricing: Free and open source (MIT); questions are generated by a model you choose (your existing coding agent, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), so you pay only for those tokens

tools.name: Reticle
tools.description: Verification layer for AI coding agents: a dev-only SDK inside your web or desktop app lets the agent drive real flows and read network calls, app state and console, then returns a pass, fail or cannot-tell verdict with the file and line to fix; saved flows replay without an AI model and can gate CI.
key_features: Embeddable SDK packages are Apache-2.0; the server, init and test packages are FSL-1.1-ALv2 (free for internal use, Apache-2.0 after two years); the hosted platform at app.reticle.sh is free to start with no credit card; enterprise features need a paid licence (price not listed publicly)

tools.name: ClipTalk

Give it a prompt, script, product, website, photo or link and it writes the script, generates the visuals, adds a voiceover from 140+ AI voices in 30+ languages, word-by-word captions, B-roll and music, then renders a ready-to-post MP4. You can edit any scene by asking in plain language, clone your own voice, cast AI characters, and on Pro use its API and MCP access for Claude and ChatGPT.

tools.name: GoldRush MCP
tools.description: Covalent's GoldRush multichain data API with an MCP server, giving agents wallet balances, transactions, token and NFT data across 100+ chains.
key_features: 14-day free trial, then from $10/mo; x402 pay per request

tools.name: Helius MCP
tools.description: Helius's MCP server for Solana: agents read accounts, transactions, tokens and NFTs through Helius RPC and APIs.
key_features: Free plan; paid plans on site
tools.pricing: Free plan; paid plans on site

tools.name: Santiment
tools.description: Crypto market intelligence on on-chain, social and development activity, with an AI assistant and API that agents can use for research.

tools.name: thirdweb Nebula
tools.description: thirdweb's AI for onchain work: agents read live chain data, analyze transactions and can buy, swap and send crypto from connected wallets.

tools.name: Coinbase Agentic Wallet MCP
tools.description: Coinbase's MCP server and wallet app (formerly Payments MCP) that let agents hold USDC and pay for x402 services on Base, Polygon and Solana within spend limits you set.

tools.name: Alby MCP
tools.description: Open-source MCP server that connects a Bitcoin Lightning wallet to your agent via Nostr Wallet Connect, so it can pay and create invoices.

tools.name: Forta Firewall
tools.description: Forta's pre-execution firewall that screens transactions for exploits and malicious activity and can block them before they settle onchain.

tools.name: Bitquery MCP
tools.description: Bitquery's hosted, read-only MCP server with 300+ tools for DEX trades, candles, wallet history and money-flow tracing across 40+ chains.
key_features: Free tier with a Bitquery account; metered on your plan

tools.description: The Graph's Token API MCP server that lets agents query token metadata, balances, transfers and holder stats in plain language.

tools.name: Messari Copilot
tools.description: Blockworks AI (formerly Messari Copilot) is an AI research copilot for crypto, answering questions from Blockworks Research and Messari research, news and market data, with an API and hosted MCP server for agents.
key_features: Enterprise plan (Messari moved to Blockworks AI); Copilot API also pay-per-request via x402
tools.pricing: Enterprise plan (Messari moved to Blockworks AI); Copilot API also pay-per-request via x402

tools.name: Blockaid
tools.description: Onchain security platform used by wallets and exchanges: transaction simulation and scanning that blocks malicious dApps, tokens and signatures before users or agents sign.

tools.name: Moralis MCP
tools.description: Moralis's MCP server that gives agents wallet, token, NFT and DeFi data across EVM chains and Solana in plain language.
key_features: Free plan; paid plans on site
tools.pricing: Free plan; paid plans on site

tools.name: Playable Notes
tools.description: Playable Notes is an AI music tool for piano teachers: snap a photo, screenshot or PDF of piano sheet music and it reads it into a real, playable score, then rearranges it for your student from a plain-language request like "easier left hand", "take out the octaves" or "put it in C". You can hear it, fix any note, print a clean PDF and share practice links, and it also works inside ChatGPT.
key_features: Freemium: 50 free credits on sign-up (1 credit reads one line of music) and editing, AI arranging (up to 100 a day), playback and printing are free; credit packs from $10 for 100 credits, as listed on its site
tools.pricing: Freemium: 50 free credits on sign-up (1 credit reads one line of music) and editing, AI arranging (up to 100 a day), playback and printing are free; credit packs from $10 for 100 credits, as listed on its site

tools.name: Metix AI
tools.description: Metix AI (formerly OpenJobs AI) is an AI recruiting platform built around Mira, an AI recruiter agent: you describe the role and Mira searches 900M+ profiles in 190+ countries, runs personalized outreach only after you approve it, handles replies and screening, and books interview-ready candidates on your calendar, often within 24 hours. You still approve outreach and run the interviews.
key_features: Paid: free 14-day trial (1 AI Agent and 500 Credits, no card required), then subscription plans from $99/month (Starter, 5,000 Credits and 1 AI Agent) up to Scale at $499/month, plus a Delivery service; prices as listed on its site
tools.pricing: Paid: free 14-day trial (1 AI Agent and 500 Credits, no card required), then subscription plans from $99/month (Starter, 5,000 Credits and 1 AI Agent) up to Scale at $499/month, plus a Delivery service; prices as listed on its site

tools.name: GMapsScraper.AI
tools.description: GMapsScraper.AI is an AI-powered Google Maps scraper for lead generation: enter keywords and it pulls business listings with names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, social links, ratings, reviews, photos and opening hours, exported to CSV or JSON. It also offers a REST API and a remote MCP server (/api/mcp) so AI agents in Claude, Cursor or OpenAI can run Google Maps searches directly.
key_features: Freemium: free plan with 1,000 credits per month (1 credit = 1 business), then Starter $29/month (50,000 credits), Pro $99/month (300,000) and Business $199/month (1,000,000), plus on-demand credits from $15 per 15,000; prices as listed on its site
tools.pricing: Freemium: free plan with 1,000 credits per month (1 credit = 1 business), then Starter $29/month (50,000 credits), Pro $99/month (300,000) and Business $199/month (1,000,000), plus on-demand credits from $15 per 15,000; prices as listed on its site

tools.name: superagnt
tools.description: superagnt is a marketing plugin for Claude and ChatGPT that helps businesses find customers through outbound, SEO and ads. With it, your AI can find the people worth reaching and load them into your outbound, see what you and your competitors rank for, and see the ads your competitors run.
key_features: Paid: free 7-day trial with no card ($3 of data credits and Growth limits), then Starter $49/month, Growth $149/month or Scale $399/month, each with monthly data credits included; Enterprise is custom; prices as listed on its site
tools.pricing: Paid: free 7-day trial with no card ($3 of data credits and Growth limits), then Starter $49/month, Growth $149/month or Scale $399/month, each with monthly data credits included; Enterprise is custom; prices as listed on its site

tools.name: Claude Duet
tools.description: Claude Duet is Anthropic's proactive personal agent app, in research preview. You message it like an assistant: it sends a morning brief from your connected apps, keeps watch on your inbox, calendar and follow-ups through the day, and only pings you when something needs you. You can also hand it tasks, from scheduling meetings to building dashboards or simple web apps, and it keeps working when you step away but checks with you before acting on your behalf. It runs on iOS, Android and claude.ai, starting with a waitlist for US Pro and Max subscribers on their existing plan limits.
key_features: Research preview by waitlist for US Pro and Max plans
tools.pricing: Research preview by waitlist for US Pro and Max plans

tools.name: 1Password for Agents
tools.description: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents sign in to your accounts without ever seeing your passwords or one-time codes. When a supported agent reaches a sign-in page, it asks for a credential from your vault; you approve the request, and 1Password fills it straight into the site, so the secret never enters the model or its memory. You can see and manage which agents have access to what. It launched with integrations for agents such as Claude Duet, ChatGPT Work and dots, Meta's Muse and Grok Bot, and needs a 1Password plan.

tools.name: PhoneUse
tools.description: PhoneUse gives AI agents phones of their own to operate. Agents get cloud Android phones that boot in seconds and scale to hundreds, or real retail iPhones and Androids in a San Francisco rack, tapped by a robot stylus, for apps that detect emulators, with real carrier numbers for SMS and 2FA codes. One MCP server with tools such as acquire, read screen, tap, type, swipe, open app and read SMS plugs into Claude, Cursor, Codex or Windsurf, and there is a Python SDK and REST API. On-demand cloud phones are billed per minute, with flat monthly prices for dedicated and real phones.
key_features: Cloud phones $0.30 per minute on demand; dedicated and real phones monthly
tools.pricing: Cloud phones $0.30 per minute on demand; dedicated and real phones monthly

tools.name: Needle
tools.description: Needle is an outbound engine built for AI agents to drive. You connect it to Claude, ChatGPT or Grok and describe who you want to reach in one prompt; it finds leads from LinkedIn, Instagram and Google Maps, enriches them with context for personal messages, and reaches out from your own connected accounts on whichever channel the lead uses, with sending limits built in. It works for sales, partnerships, hiring or fundraising outreach, and you can start for free.

tools.name: BAND
tools.description: BAND is an interaction layer for teams running many AI agents alongside people. Agents and humans share one chat-like workspace where they coordinate tasks, exchange context and hand off work in real time, with governance over how agents communicate built in, instead of hand-wiring every handoff. BAND for Developers connects coding agents across your existing development tools so they can work together without you acting as their project manager.

tools.name: UseIt Studio
tools.description: UseIt Studio is an AI design agent for things you can hold. You describe what you want in a sentence, it asks the questions a designer would, and you refine any detail by pointing at it. Instead of a flat mockup you get a real, editable design file ready to print, cut and fold, with true dimensions, bleed and dielines, for pins, stickers, gift boxes, pop-up cards, packaging and brand kits. It runs in the browser, and a Windows desktop helper lets you call it up anywhere.

tools.name: Voxtral 3
tools.description: Voxtral 3 is Mistral AI's voice agent stack: speech-to-text in 50+ languages with speaker labels and end-of-turn detection, expressive text-to-speech in 35+ languages, and a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit that handles listening, tool calls and speaking in one stream over SIP or WebRTC. You can use it through Mistral's API with EU, US or global endpoints, or deploy it yourself, and it is priced per minute of audio or per character.
key_features: Transcription from $0.0035/min, TTS $13 per 1M characters, voice agent API from $0.04/min
tools.pricing: Transcription from $0.0035/min, TTS $13 per 1M characters, voice agent API from $0.04/min

tools.name: Mercury 3
tools.description: Mercury 3 is Inception's diffusion language model, which writes many tokens in parallel rather than one at a time, reaching over 1,000 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs with a 1M-token context, tool calling and structured outputs. It has an OpenAI-compatible API and is also offered on OpenRouter, Baseten and Vercel, which makes it a fit for voice bots, support agents and browser agents where response speed matters. Pricing is per million input and output tokens.

tools.name: OmniRush
tools.description: OmniRush is a desktop coding agent for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a terminal CLI as well. It works through the files of your own projects, reading code, making edits and running commands, and gives free access to frontier models from a model picker, with GPT 6 Astra as the default. Builds for each platform are published on its releases page.
key_features: Free desktop app with free frontier-model access
tools.pricing: Free desktop app with free frontier-model access

tools.name: Unreal Agent
tools.description: Unreal Agent is an async-first agent harness from Unreal Labs, a team researching how to make agentic workflows efficient. The library handles inputs with stable IDs and deduplication, append-only sessions that can be forked, and a coordinator that manages each model turn and translates tool calls into operations. It ships with a cloud agent runner, a terminal UI and benchmark runners, under the MIT license.

tools.name: MemoraX Code
tools.description: MemoraX Code is a shared memory layer for coding agents such as Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Trae and DeepSeek Harness. It recalls prior engineering knowledge, captures lessons from finished work, keeps repository knowledge and architecture history up to date, and carries your procedures and preferences into new sessions, bringing back only the memory relevant to the task at hand. It needs Node.js 20 or later and is MIT licensed.

tools.name: AOCI-CODE
tools.description: AOCI-CODE keeps a persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase and database schema that your coding agent writes and a local MCP server governs. Agents in Codex, Claude Code, Cursor or OpenCode read the map once and know what each file is for, what it depends on and what must not break, instead of re-reading the repo on every task. It can index an existing codebase of up to about half a million lines and report how well it knows each area before taking over development.

tools.name: OpenHarness
tools.description: OpenHarness from Autonomous is a native command center for running coding agents side by side, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Devin, Amp and Copilot. It links your laptop, home server and GPU box into one window with a password instead of SSH keys or port forwarding, keeps code and keystrokes end-to-end encrypted through its relay, and is keyboard first. Agents keep working when you close it, and it extends beyond code to CAD, circuits, robots, games and music.

tools.name: Wisp Science
tools.description: Wisp Science is an open-source, local-first AI research workbench for scientists on Windows, macOS and Linux. Its agent searches the literature, runs persistent Python and R kernels on your laptop or remote servers, queries about 80 scientific databases and loads reusable skills, while keeping figures, runs, decisions and drafts together in one project. You bring your own OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic model, or drive Codex or Claude Code, and approval gates stay on by default.

tools.name: Foreman
tools.description: Foreman from ThruWire supervises coding agents with fast decision models. You give it a ticket, spec or bug report and it runs Codex, OpenCode, Hermes or LangChain's Deep Agents Code as workers, or attaches to supported sessions such as Pi, then independently judges whether the job meets the original requirements, whether the test evidence is enough and when verification or human input is needed. Extra checks can be configured for your workflow, and it is MIT licensed.

tools.name: FableCut
tools.description: FableCut is a Premiere-style video editor that runs entirely in the browser and exposes the whole timeline as one JSON document, covering media, clips, tracks, effects, keyframes and transitions. You can edit by hand or let an AI agent such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop cut the video over MCP or REST while the timeline updates live. It has no npm dependencies, starts with one node command and is MIT licensed.

tools.name: Diagrid Catalyst MCP
tools.description: The Diagrid Catalyst MCP server lets AI coding agents build and operate Dapr Workflows and Dapr durable agents on Diagrid Catalyst, the managed platform for long-running, fault-tolerant agent and workflow apps. Through it an agent can create and inspect workflows, check running instances and manage Catalyst resources from your MCP client. It is the official server from Diagrid, the company behind Dapr, and needs a Catalyst sign-in.

tools.name: Cayu
tools.description: Cayu is an open-source Python framework for building and running domain-specific, long-horizon agents on a durable runtime. Sessions survive restarts and redeploys from SQLite or Postgres stores, tool policies can require human approval before side effects, spend caps are checked before each model call, and timers, background tasks, subagents and forks cover longer multi-agent work. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.

tools.name: Inngest
tools.description: Inngest is a durable workflow orchestration platform for running stateful step functions and AI workflows on serverless, servers or the edge. You write functions in TypeScript, Python or Go with automatic retries, queues, throttling and human-in-the-loop waits, and its AgentKit and AI inference steps let you build durable, long-running AI agents with tracing and evals. The server is source-available (SSPL, converting to Apache 2.0 later) and can be self-hosted, or you can use Inngest Cloud.
key_features: Inngest Cloud: Free $0/mo (50k executions, 5 seats), Pro $99/mo, Business $499/mo, Enterprise custom (inngest.com/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Server is source-available (SSPL with delayed Apache 2.0) and self-hostable.
tools.pricing: Inngest Cloud: Free $0/mo (50k executions, 5 seats), Pro $99/mo, Business $499/mo, Enterprise custom (inngest.com/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Server is source-available (SSPL with delayed Apache 2.0) and self-hostable.

tools.name: Windmill
tools.description: Windmill is an open-source developer platform that turns scripts in Python, TypeScript, Go, SQL and other languages into webhooks, workflows and internal UIs. Its flows include AI agent steps that call an LLM with your scripts as tools, support nested agents and MCP, and run on a fast self-hostable workflow engine. It positions itself as an open-source alternative to Retool and Temporal.
key_features: Free and open-source Community Edition from $0/mo (self-hosted, unlimited executions, up to 10 SSO users); Enterprise from $120/mo; cloud and self-hosted paid plans (windmill.dev/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Core is AGPLv3, some enterprise features proprietary.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source Community Edition from $0/mo (self-hosted, unlimited executions, up to 10 SSO users); Enterprise from $120/mo; cloud and self-hosted paid plans (windmill.dev/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026). Core is AGPLv3, some enterprise features proprietary.

tools.name: Kestra
tools.description: Kestra is an open-source, event-driven orchestration and scheduling platform where workflows are declared in YAML or built in a no-code editor. It includes an AI Agent task that gives flows an LLM with memory and tools, supports nested agents and the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, and can expose any flow as a tool to external AI agents through its MCP server. It runs in the cloud, on-prem or air-gapped and is Apache 2.0 licensed.
key_features: Open Source edition is free (Apache 2.0); Enterprise Edition and Kestra Cloud are annual subscriptions priced via sales, no public price (kestra.io/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026).
tools.pricing: Open Source edition is free (Apache 2.0); Enterprise Edition and Kestra Cloud are annual subscriptions priced via sales, no public price (kestra.io/pricing, checked Oct 22 2026).

tools.name: FloGPT
tools.description: FloGPT is an AI chat and voice agent platform with a built-in AI CRM: embed a chat widget on your website, run AI phone agents around the clock, and handle chat, voice, email, SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook conversations from one inbox, all grounded in your own knowledge base.
key_features: Freemium: free plan ($0/month plus usage for calls and SMS, 100 messages), then Starter $49/month, Growth $149/month or Professional $399/month, each plus usage for calls and SMS; prices as listed on its site
tools.pricing: Freemium: free plan ($0/month plus usage for calls and SMS, 100 messages), then Starter $49/month, Growth $149/month or Professional $399/month, each plus usage for calls and SMS; prices as listed on its site

tools.name: Reference to Video
tools.description: Reference to Video turns product photos into 6-second AI ad clips for ecommerce and social: upload a product image, pick a shot style (showcase, lifestyle UGC, close-up detail or slow camera move) and an aspect ratio, and get a vertical, landscape or square video in 480p or 720p. Its reference mode treats the photo as a strict guide for tighter product fidelity and camera control.
key_features: Paid: no free plan; one-time credit packs from $4.99 for 400 credits or $9.99 for 900 credits (valid 365 days), plus monthly and yearly plans; each 6-second clip costs 80-240 credits depending on mode and resolution; prices as listed on its site
tools.pricing: Paid: no free plan; one-time credit packs from $4.99 for 400 credits or $9.99 for 900 credits (valid 365 days), plus monthly and yearly plans; each 6-second clip costs 80-240 credits depending on mode and resolution; prices as listed on its site

tools.name: Motion Transfer
tools.description: Motion Transfer animates a character photo by copying the movement from a reference video: the photo sets the look while the clip drives gestures, expressions and body motion. Upload your own 4-30 second clip or pick a ready-made motion template, choose the model, resolution, length and aspect ratio in settings, see a credit estimate first, then preview and download the result. It also includes general AI image and video generation from one shared credit balance.
key_features: Freemium: free Basic plan with one-time signup credits (the site banner advertises 60; the pricing page lists 18) and watermarked downloads; Starter $8.30/month billed yearly ($100/year, 2,400 credits), Pro $30/month billed yearly ($49.90 month-to-month), Business $49.90/month billed yearly; prices as listed on its site
tools.pricing: Freemium: free Basic plan with one-time signup credits (the site banner advertises 60; the pricing page lists 18) and watermarked downloads; Starter $8.30/month billed yearly ($100/year, 2,400 credits), Pro $30/month billed yearly ($49.90 month-to-month), Business $49.90/month billed yearly; prices as listed on its site

tools.name: Teebots
tools.description: Teebots is a free desktop app that keeps a small team of AI bots on your own computer. Each bot can use a different model through your own API key, with requests going straight to the provider, and keeps its own private memory alongside a shared group memory. Put several bots in one group chat and @mention one to hand it a task, or let them pass steps to each other. Bots can work with files in their own folder, run commands, use skills including MCP and browse in their own browser, but they stop and wait for your approval before submitting or paying for anything. Scheduled daily or weekly jobs keep running from the menu bar. Chats, memory, files and logins stay local. Available for Mac (Apple silicon) now, with Windows and Linux coming soon.
key_features: Free: the app costs nothing; model usage is billed to the API key you add. macOS (Apple silicon, v0.1.2) now; Windows and Linux coming soon
tools.pricing: Free: the app costs nothing; model usage is billed to the API key you add. macOS (Apple silicon, v0.1.2) now; Windows and Linux coming soon

tools.name: HaveTML
tools.description: HaveTML lets AI agents publish what they make as a permanent share link. Ask Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to publish HTML, Markdown, JSON or YAML, and you get a sandboxed link anyone can open without logging in. Each link keeps its version history, supports comments, and can be set to private, unlisted or public.

tools.name: PeekPanda
tools.description: PeekPanda is competitor research for iOS apps. Open any app to see the Meta ads it keeps paying for and how long each has run, the US App Store searches it ranks for, and which of its posts went viral. Use it in the web app, or add its MCP server so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can answer questions about any iOS competitor.

tools.name: HireDov
tools.description: HireDov is an AI sourcing agent. Describe what you need to buy and its agent, Dov, finds qualified suppliers, sends each a tailored request for quote in their own language, chases every reply and brings the quotes back to one dashboard to compare; first quotes usually arrive within a few days. You see the suppliers it finds before you pay.

tools.name: System One API
tools.description: System One API is the hosted decision API behind TypeSafe Jev, with an open-source TypeScript SDK for AI agents. Where the TypeSafe Jev listing covers the decision model itself, this listing covers the developer API and console: send text or app context and get back a typed choice, a score or a yes/no probability for routing tools, ranking results and checking conditions, with API keys, call logs and credit use managed in one place.
key_features: 100 free credits on sign-up; Starter $10 for 10,000 prepaid credits; no subscription
tools.pricing: 100 free credits on sign-up; Starter $10 for 10,000 prepaid credits; no subscription

tools.name: Financial Cents MCP
tools.description: The Financial Cents MCP server connects an accounting, bookkeeping or tax firm's Financial Cents practice-management account to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and other MCP clients. Staff can ask about overdue work, unpaid invoices or missing client tax documents in plain English and have the assistant log time or create tasks, with each connection bound to one firm, your own permissions applied, writes confirmed in the client and deletes not offered at all. It is a hosted server signed in with OAuth and comes with the Scale plan.

tools.name: Userpilot Agent Analytics
tools.description: Userpilot Agent Analytics shows product teams how users actually get on with the AI agent inside their app. It reads the agent's conversations at scale and reports whether people got what they needed or left frustrated, so teams can see where the agent fails, which requests it can't handle and how agent use ties back to product engagement, alongside Userpilot's existing product analytics.

tools.name: Tulimoa Memory
tools.description: Tulimoa Memory is a hosted, shared memory store for AI agents and agent swarms. Agents write what they learn into it during the day; overnight a separate model sorts those notes into a knowledge graph with associative recall, and each agent starts the morning with a short briefing so it reads less and knows more. It is billed per call, with starting credit to try it.

tools.name: Keboola MCP Server
tools.description: Keboola's official MCP server lets AI assistants and coding agents work with a Keboola data project: browse storage tables and buckets, read and write SQL transformations, run and debug jobs and components, and build data flows from a chat. It can run locally or as Keboola's hosted remote server, with access scoped to the project token or OAuth sign-in you grant.

tools.name: Speakeasy Gram
tools.description: Gram is Speakeasy's open-source platform for building, hosting and governing MCP servers. Teams can turn APIs into curated MCP toolsets, host them, and manage which agents and people may use which servers from one control plane, with sign-in, access policies and usage visibility; its own MCP server lets an agent manage that setup directly.

tools.name: SuprSend MCP
tools.description: SuprSend's official hosted MCP server gives AI agents and coding assistants access to a SuprSend notification workspace. An agent can look up and manage users and lists, inspect and edit notification workflows and templates, and read delivery data across email, SMS, push, Slack and in-app inbox channels without leaving the chat or editor.
key_features: Free plan $0/month (10k notifications/mo, no card); Essentials from $100/month billed annually; Business and Enterprise tiers
tools.pricing: Free plan $0/month (10k notifications/mo, no card); Essentials from $100/month billed annually; Business and Enterprise tiers

tools.name: Edgegap MCP
tools.description: Edgegap's official MCP server lets AI coding agents deploy and run multiplayer game servers on Edgegap's edge hosting network. From the editor, an agent can push server builds, start and stop deployments, check matchmaking and fleet status and read logs, so game developers can manage their online backend in plain language.

tools.name: Jev
tools.description: Jev is an open-source chat assistant for Android, Windows and macOS that reads the conversation on your screen, judges what the other person wants and whether a message looks risky, and drafts candidate replies for you. It fills in the reply box, but you always decide whether to send, so it helps with tricky messages without acting on its own.

tools.name: Waku
tools.description: Waku is a native desktop app that gathers your local coding agents in one place. It shows sessions from Amp, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok and Pi on a single timeline that stays entirely on your machine, so you can follow and switch between agent runs without juggling terminals.

tools.name: Paritok
tools.description: Paritok is a compression gateway that sits between a coding agent and its LLM. Using its own open-source 4B code-aware model, it shrinks tool output, files and conversation history on the fly without losing what the agent needs, which cuts token bills and lets agent sessions run longer before they hit context limits.

tools.name: Rome OS
tools.description: Rome is an open-source agent OS for recursive agents that compounds what they learn. Agents build their own tools, keep context and reuse capabilities across tasks instead of starting fresh each time, so a long-running assistant grows more capable the more it works.

tools.name: TapQ
tools.description: TapQ is an always-on voice layer for the coding and work agents you already run. You talk to Claude Code, Codex and others through your earbuds, interrupt them, steer the work and hear spoken updates, so you can supervise agents hands-free while away from the keyboard.

tools.name: nanocode
tools.description: nanocode is a small SDK for embedding frontier-model agents inside your own apps and tools. It provides the agent loop, tool calling and session handling for models such as Claude and GPT in a compact codebase, so developers can ship a capable embedded agent without adopting a heavy framework.

tools.name: 0.security
tools.description: 0 is an open, self-improving AI operating system for offensive security work. Its agents investigate code and binaries for vulnerabilities, test defenses, verify findings with working proofs and help fix the issues, and the team behind it publishes the advisories it has found in real open-source projects.

tools.name: agent-manager
tools.description: agent-manager is a terminal app built on tmux for running many AI coding agents at once. It shows live status for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Grok, Cursor and other sessions in a foldable project tree, adds a quick prompt bar, and has a diff reviewer whose line comments are sent straight back to the right agent, on macOS, Linux and Windows.

tools.name: mu
tools.description: mu is an open-source coding agent with a judgment kernel: a small, fast judge model makes the many routine decisions in each turn so the main model only gets the context it needs. It ships as a command-line tool and a desktop app and aims to keep coding sessions focused and cheap.

tools.name: Streamkap MCP
tools.description: Streamkap's official CLI and MCP server let AI agents manage real-time change-data-capture pipelines on Streamkap. An agent can create and edit sources, destinations, pipelines and transforms, check their status and troubleshoot lag, streaming database changes into warehouses and apps without clicking through the console.
key_features: Free plan $0 (500 MB/month, MCP server included); paid plans priced by data volume
tools.pricing: Free plan $0 (500 MB/month, MCP server included); paid plans priced by data volume

tools.name: Agente Smart Documents
tools.description: Agente Smart Documents turns a finished Word document into a reusable template your AI agent can fill. You upload an example, it builds the template, then ChatGPT or Codex, Claude, Grok Bot, Hermes or the web workspace asks only for the details that are missing and hands back a filled .docx with the original layout kept, for you to review before sending. A few documents are free each month, then a flat monthly fee per office.

tools.name: CutBay
tools.description: CutBay is a chat-based AI video agent that turns ideas, web links, documents, slides, spreadsheets and your own media into finished videos. You describe what you want and it drafts explainers, product demos, slideshows, animated charts, talking-head clips or YouTube Shorts, then lets you keep editing by chat, with add-ons such as B-roll and automatic subtitles.

tools.name: only-cli
tools.description: only-cli (oc) turns any website into a compact command-line view for AI agents. It distills a page into short text with numbered actions that agents like Claude Code can follow and click through, so agents browse the web using a small fraction of the tokens raw HTML or screenshots would take.

tools.name: Vidmoat
tools.description: Vidmoat is a hosted AI video editor you direct in chat. Describe the edit and its agent cuts dead air, adds word-synced captions, grades and reframes your footage on a real timeline, where you can review and change any cut by hand before rendering an MP4. It works in the browser, on Telegram (@vidmoat_bot) and over MCP (https://api.vidmoat.com/api/mcp, OAuth), so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can drive edits too.
key_features: Hobby $0 (no card, 40 AI credits/mo, 720p with watermark); Creator $19/mo; Studio $49/mo; Team $29/seat/mo (min 3 seats); day passes from $2.99
tools.pricing: Hobby $0 (no card, 40 AI credits/mo, 720p with watermark); Creator $19/mo; Studio $49/mo; Team $29/seat/mo (min 3 seats); day passes from $2.99

tools.name: SalesTouch
tools.description: SalesTouch is a LinkedIn MCP server for AI agents. Connect Claude, Codex, ChatGPT or any remote MCP client to https://www.salestouch.io/api/mcp and your agent can find prospects, research people and companies, send invitations and messages, and handle follow-ups through 45 purpose-built LinkedIn tools instead of browser automation. Scoped OAuth, approvals for sensitive actions, daily limits, working hours and a human-paced action queue keep the account under control.
key_features: $39/month or $389/year; 7-day free trial (card required, no charge before day 7); one LinkedIn account included
tools.pricing: $39/month or $389/year; 7-day free trial (card required, no charge before day 7); one LinkedIn account included

tools.name: Vellm
tools.description: Vellm turns photos of people and pets into short AI videos from ready-made templates. Pick one of 108 dance, funny, duo and pet templates built on ByteDance Seedance 2.5, upload your photos and it renders your own version, or start from a prompt in its Create Studio. A remote MCP server (https://api.vellm.app/mcp, OAuth sign-in) lets MCP-compatible AI apps create videos from your Vellm account.
key_features: One-time credit packs from $4.49 (50 credits, one video) up to $39.99 (600 credits); monthly plans $20.99 (350 credits) and $41.99 (700 credits); templates cost 50-100 credits; no free trial
tools.pricing: One-time credit packs from $4.49 (50 credits, one video) up to $39.99 (600 credits); monthly plans $20.99 (350 credits) and $41.99 (700 credits); templates cost 50-100 credits; no free trial

tools.name: Crolytics
tools.description: Crolytics is a managed, governed AI workspace for B2B marketing and go-to-market teams, hosted on Google Cloud. Its agents connect to your CMS, GA4, Search Console and knowledge base through custom MCP connectors, answer analytics questions in plain language, track how AI assistants cite your brand (GEO/AEO), and draft or update website pages behind human approval gates, with per-person permissions and a tamper-evident audit log. Teams use it from the Crolytics chat or inside their own Claude or ChatGPT account.
key_features: Growth $5,000/month (managed and run for you, no per-seat or usage pricing); Enterprise custom; every plan starts with a free 2-week pilot after a scoping call
tools.pricing: Growth $5,000/month (managed and run for you, no per-seat or usage pricing); Enterprise custom; every plan starts with a free 2-week pilot after a scoping call

tools.name: DIRI AI
tools.description: DIRI AI is a voice role-play trainer for salespeople. You pick a situation, such as a price objection, an intro meeting, a cold call or a client who wants to leave, set the difficulty, and talk out loud with an AI customer that reacts to what you actually say rather than a fixed script. After each call you get an instant report with a transcript, the key moments highlighted and specific stronger wording to try next time, plus a history of your practice. Managers can use it to help new hires ramp up before real calls.
key_features: Free €0 (no card): 1 voice call a day, up to 5 minutes, with a full report; Start €19.90/month (80 min), Plus €49.90/month (240 min), Pro €99.90/month (480 min); 7-day free trial on paid plans (card required)
tools.pricing: Free €0 (no card): 1 voice call a day, up to 5 minutes, with a full report; Start €19.90/month (80 min), Plus €49.90/month (240 min), Pro €99.90/month (480 min); 7-day free trial on paid plans (card required)

tools.name: Fileaify
tools.description: Fileaify is a project workspace that plugs into the coding agent you already use, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Windsurf. You give the agent one URL (fileaify.com/agent) or the hosted MCP connector, approve its access, and it finds the project's documentation, architecture decisions, roadmap and known issues in each new conversation, so you don't have to explain the project again, even when you switch agents. Credentials stay in a vault: the agent can run approved actions with them without ever seeing the keys, sensitive actions need a human's approval, and paid tiers add a sandboxed executor where the agent can actually run work. The agent also writes its contributions back into the project docs, following your review rules. A live demo project lets you try it without installing anything.
key_features: Free €0 (1 project, 5 services and secrets); Solo €4.90/month; Pro €14.90/month; Premium €39.90/month; Enterprise on request
tools.pricing: Free €0 (1 project, 5 services and secrets); Solo €4.90/month; Pro €14.90/month; Premium €39.90/month; Enterprise on request

tools.name: img2threejs
tools.description: img2threejs is an open-source agent workflow that looks at a reference image and rebuilds the object in it as a procedural Three.js model written purely in code. Each model goes through quality gates before it is accepted, comes out ready to animate, and is built in a token-efficient way, so a coding agent can turn photos or concept art into live 3D scenes without any mesh files.

tools.name: Waggle
tools.description: Waggle shows which files an AI agent actually opened before it answered. Instead of pasting whole documents between agents, it hands over short references that can be traced back to the source, so you can check whether an answer was grounded in what you gave the agent and send it back when it skipped the reading. It plugs into agent harnesses over MCP.

tools.name: Strands Decider
tools.description: Strands Decider is a small, fast decision model from Strands Labs for agent workflows. Rather than asking a full LLM every time, an agent can use it to choose between options or score something on a scale in a fraction of the time, with calibrated confidence so the workflow knows when to fall back to a bigger model.

tools.name: Decionis
tools.description: Decionis is an approval gateway for actions taken by AI agents. It sits in front of consequential API calls such as payments, price changes and orders, checks each one against your policy before it runs, and only lets it through with a single-use permit, keeping a signed record of every decision for audit.

tools.name: Foremerge
tools.description: Foremerge is an open-source coordination layer for teams of coding agents, built on top of Git. Each agent keeps its own worktree, but they share what they intend to change, claim the parts of the code they are working on and verify each other's change sets, so conflicting plans are caught before they turn into merge conflicts. It also works over MCP.

tools.name: CodeAF
tools.description: CodeAF is an open-source software factory from AgentField built to run on open models. It ships ready-made specialist agents you call with slash commands, one to build features like a senior developer, one to audit code for security issues and one to review GitHub pull requests, and spreads the work across a pool of models to balance cost and quality.

tools.name: Kition
tools.description: Kition is an open-source desktop office workspace with an AI agent built in. It combines documents, data tables and a whiteboard for design work in one app, and its tool-using agent can research the web, write and translate, organise records and produce editable brand assets, with visual workflows to chain the steps together.

tools.name: BeefTV
tools.description: BeefTV is an open-source, local-first desktop workspace for making AI video. On a free-form canvas you connect footage, images, generation models and agents into one flow, so you can go from an idea to finished clips without hopping between tools. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.

tools.name: Aletheore
tools.description: Aletheore audits code repositories and backs every finding with evidence. Its deterministic scanner looks for leaked secrets, vulnerable dependencies and dead code, it can watch live endpoints and draw architecture maps, and it reviews pull requests automatically through a GitHub Action. A built-in MCP server lets coding agents run the same audits.

tools.name: Tura
tools.description: Tura is an open-source agent runtime focused on cutting LLM spending. It manages the context an agent sends to the model so tasks use far fewer tokens, while keeping the finished results, execution evidence and benchmark scores auditable, which makes it aimed at teams running agents at scale.

tools.name: PartMode
tools.description: PartMode is open-source parametric 3D CAD that runs in the browser and is built to be driven by both people and AI agents. You can create multi-part designs and assemblies with lofts, sweeps and mates, browse a shared parts library, and export to STEP, STL, AMF or 3MF, while a command-line interface lets agents make permissioned changes. No account is needed.

tools.name: Machinist
tools.description: Machinist is an open-source software factory for coding agents. It runs agent jobs on your laptop, a virtual machine or a Kubernetes cluster, connects to GitHub so you can review the changes they make, and automates routine repository upkeep such as dependency bumps and fixes, with evals to check the results.

tools.name: Concord
tools.description: Concord lets coding agents message each other and work together in a shared workspace. Agents running in different tools or on different machines can hand off tasks, ask each other questions and review each other's code in real time through its MCP server, so a team of agents can coordinate without you copying messages between terminals.

tools.name: JSON2Video MCP
tools.description: The official JSON2Video MCP server lets AI agents produce videos through the JSON2Video API. An agent can render a movie from a JSON description, check on render status, validate the JSON before sending it and use ready-made templates, which makes it a fit for automated video production at scale; a free credit allowance is included.

tools.name: ClicData MCP
tools.description: ClicData's MCP server connects its data platform to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. You ask about churn, revenue or pipeline in plain language and get real analysis, live charts and full dashboards built from the governed business data you already keep in ClicData, which suits mid-sized teams without a data engineering group.

tools.name: Shadeform
tools.description: Shadeform is a marketplace for on-demand GPUs across more than 30 cloud providers, now with an official CLI and MCP server. AI agents can compare prices, launch and manage GPU instances and scale inference through one API, instead of you signing up to each cloud separately.

tools.name: SecureAuth MCP Authority
tools.description: SecureAuth MCP Authority is a security gateway for the MCP tool calls agents make. Every call is checked against the person the agent is acting for, using that person's own login and rules down to individual arguments, and each decision is logged so enterprises can see and control what their agents are allowed to do.

tools.name: SimpleBackups MCP
tools.description: The official SimpleBackups MCP server lets AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor and Codex manage your backups. From a chat you can check the status of server, database and storage backups, dig into failed runs and set up or automate backup jobs on your SimpleBackups account.

tools.name: ChatAcademia
tools.description: ChatAcademia is a set of AI research agents for academics. Its agents search many scholarly databases, pull insights out of papers and help with each step from forming an idea to drafting a publication, and a desktop app can work directly with the research documents on your own computer.

tools.name: EnhanceWizard
tools.description: EnhanceWizard is a browser-based AI image enhancer and upscaler that sharpens, unblurs, denoises and restores photos at original size, 2x or 4x. Its free browser tier processes images locally on your device up to 16 MP (8,192 px per side) with no sign-up, daily limit or watermark; optional cloud credits unlock Standard HD batch jobs up to 10 images and AI Retouch.

tools.pricing: Free $0 (no card, unlimited local browser processing up to 16 MP with no watermark); 50-credit pack $9 (one-time, valid 12 months); Monthly $12/month (100 credits/month)

tools.name: Pudding
tools.description: Pudding is a desktop AI workspace from Teatak for macOS and Windows 11 that connects your own model API keys or local Ollama models with a built-in browser, file and command tools, a Studio for Markdown documents and typed tables, scheduled tasks, parallel subtask delegation and MCP plugins. Every tool call is shown in the conversation with per-project permission controls (Ask, Auto or Full access).
key_features: Free desktop app for personal and commercial use (no account required; agent core Apache-2.0); model providers and external services charge separately
tools.pricing: Free desktop app for personal and commercial use (no account required; agent core Apache-2.0); model providers and external services charge separately

tools.name: Orbi
tools.description: Orbi is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) software factory for GitHub repositories. When you label a GitHub Issue ai-ready, Orbi implements it in an isolated worktree, opens and reviews pull requests in a separate AI review session that checks acceptance criteria and repairs failing tests, merges the exact reviewed commit SHA, and cuts a tagged GitHub Release when a human applies the ai-release label.

tools.pricing: Self-hosted: free and open source (AGPL-3.0 or Sustainable Use License, bring your own model); Cloud: 3 free merged deliveries (no card), Solo $24/month (400M tokens, 1 repo), Pro $66/month (1.2B tokens, 5 repos)

tools.name: Sora2 Hub
tools.description: Sora2 Hub is a third-party multi-model web studio (not affiliated with OpenAI) for generating AI images and videos from text prompts or reference images. It brings together 10+ video and image models—including Sora 2, Veo 3.1, Kling AI, Runway, Hailuo 2.3, GPT-4o Image, Flux Kontext and Nano Banana Pro—alongside a prompt library and 2,000+ visual effects.

tools.description: Massvai is an AI full-stack app builder for Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Supabase.
